# parity-fuzz --mode nest baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode nest --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# FIXED (no longer gaps): the DQ scalar-collapse of a nested inner SET/ZIP
# operator. Inside `"…"` (or a nested inner running under the outer's ssub
# scalar context), the `:^` / `:^^` zip now collapses its LEFT operand to a
# sepjoined scalar BEFORE zipping — `"${${a:^b}}"` is `1 2 3 a`, matching zsh
# (c:Src/subst.c:3032, gated on SUBEXP_SCALAR_CTX like the `:|`/`:*` arms).
# The `(@)` flag (nojoin=2) correctly suppresses that collapse (per-element).
#
# FIXED (no longer gaps): `${#${#s}}` after a flag expansion on an
# array/assoc (`${(U)arr}`, `${(o)a}`, …). PARAMSUBST_LF_ARRAY leaked the
# prior call's array-ness into the getlen early-return, so the outer `${#…}`
# counted the inner scalar length as 1 ELEMENT instead of 2 CHARS. Fixed by
# resetting PARAMSUBST_LF_ARRAY to the non-array default at the top of every
# paramsubst (c:Src/subst.c:3932). The two `${#${#s}}` signatures below were
# removed once fixed so a regression re-flags as NEW.
#
# One remaining known gap: an (s::)/split that yields ONLY EMPTY fields,
# nested under another flag in DQ (`"${(L)${(s.:.)${t[2]}}}"` where t[2] is a
# lone `:`). zsh's prefork deletes the empty nodes in the SUBEXP multsub pass
# (→ empty result `[]`), whereas the port keeps them and sepjoins to a single
# space (`[ ]`). Narrow edge (splitting a lone delimiter, nested, quoted);
# the DIRECT `"${(s.:.):}"` form matches (both a single space).
print -r -- "[${(L)${(s.:.)${t[N]}}}]"
